ai.description: This 20–25 mm frog is brown with a distinct pale mid-dorsal stripe. It features a wrinkled, granular dorsum and prominent, fleshy toe pads. It belongs to the family Nyctibatrachidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus minor* is best distinguished by its significantly smaller size and the presence of prominent, longitudinal skin folds on its dorsum compared to larger congeners.
ai.habitat: *Nyctibatrachus minor* inhabits evergreen forests and riparian zones in the Western Ghats, typically found near rocky streams at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Small Wrinkled Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining active at night to forage for small invertebrates along the rocky streams of the Western Ghats.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus minor* breeds during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of 15–30 eggs directly on wet rocks near streams, where they undergo direct development.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus minor* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically found at elevations between 700 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The *Nyctibatrachus minor* produces a series of high-pitched, insect-like chirps, typically heard while the frogs are perched on rocks near fast-flowing forest streams.
